High-period swell waves from the southern Indian Ocean reached the southern tip of the country on Saturday and began interacting with the coastal regions, the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) confirmed.
Swell waves with a period of 20 to 24 seconds and a height of up to 1.5 metres reportedly hit parts of Kanyakumari, while precursor waves — minor wave patterns that travel ahead of the main swell — began reaching the Keralam coast, said the KSDMA.
Possibility of inundation
The impact of the swell surge (Kallakadal) is expected to become more pronounced from Saturday night, particularly during the high-tide period. The swell system is expected to continue interacting with the coast and coastal regions until 2.30 a.m. on September 28, with a possibility of inundation in low-lying coastal areas of Keralam.
A red alert has been issued along the Keralam coast suspending all recreational and fishing activities until September 28, while a cell-broadcast warning message was sent to mobile phones of people across the coastal regions of the State on Friday night.
The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), which provides forecasts on ocean conditions in the seas surrounding India during extreme weather events such as high waves, swells and cyclones, has issued a swell surge warning for Keralam, southern Tamil Nadu and Lakshadweep from September 26 to 28.
According to INCOIS, the event originated approximately 10,000 km from the Indian coast in the southern Indian Ocean on September 20 and is gradually propagating towards the northern Indian Ocean. This has resulted in the propagation of high-energy swells, with a peak wave period of around 23 seconds, towards the Indian coastal regions. These long-period swells, combined with high-tide conditions, may cause coastal flooding in low-lying areas of Keralam, the southern Tamil Nadu districts and the Lakshadweep islands during the forecast period.
Advisory to fishers
Fishermen and coastal residents in Keralam have been advised to remain alert to intermittent surges of seawater in nearshore and beach areas, particularly in low-lying locations. The public and fishermen have been advised not to operate small vessels close to shore. Boats should be anchored at a safe distance from one another to prevent collisions and damage. All operational and recreational activities, including tourism activities, along the beaches and nearshore areas have also been suspended.

Maharashtra announces relief measures in drought—Restructures crop loans, concessions in pump electric bills; check list Maharashtra has activated ‘Trigger-1’ under its Drought Management Code 2016 to initiate relief measures in drought-affected areas. We take a look at the financial relief measures announced by the state government. The Maharashtra government today declared drought in 74% or 265 of 358 talukas of the state amid deficit in rainfall, PTI reported. Prior to this, in a government resolution dated late on Friday, 25 September, the state listed the 32 affected districts, with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar division having the highest number of affected talukas, at 74. The government in its order on Saturday, 26 September, announced relief measures, such as crop loan restructuring, land revenue concessions, and power bill subsidies. Further, it noted that financial assistance for crop losses will be announced after the prescribed procedure in a separate GR. Drought Management Code's ‘Trigger-1’ activated Notably, the state has activated ‘Trigger-1’ under the state Drought Management Code 2016 (updated in 2020) to declare drought conditions and initiate relief. This is the first stage in Maharashtra's drought framework, which is activated in case of rainfall deficit of 25% and prolonged dry spell of 21 days combined. The report said Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar division has the highest number of drought-affected talukas — 74, followed by Amravati — 56, Nashik — 49, Nagpur — 39, Pune — 35, and Thane — 12. Other districts on the list include, Sindhudurg — 8, Ratnagiri — 3, and Raigad — 1, the report added. What are the relief measures announced? The state has announced a number of relief measures as follows: Land revenue concessions, Restructuring of crop loans, Postponement of recovery of agriculture-related loans and Concessions in agricultural pump electricity bills. Electricity bills of agricultural pumps up to 7.5 horsepower had already been waived and will now also apply to pumps above that capacity in affected areas. The report added that state Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharne said officials will conduct accurate and transparent panchnamas (crop-loss surveys), undertake crop-cutting experiments on an urgent basis and ensure that farmers receive benefits under crop insurance and various government schemes. “It is extremely painful to watch standing crops being lost before the eyes of farmers. Therefore, we do not want to stop at merely declaring drought, but want to ensure that actual assistance reaches farmers,” Bharne said. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Saturday told the officials to expedite the process of restoration of power supply in the areas that received heavy rains due to the deep depression in the Bay of Bengal and to distribute 50 kg of rice free of cost to each one of the fisherfolk families who could not venture into the sea for the last five days.
Taking stock of the situation in a teleconference along with Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu and Chief Secretary G. Sai Prasad and other senior officials, Mr. Naidu said Vamsadhara water should be diverted into the Hiramandalam reservoir to utilise the floodwaters to the extent possible.
‘Assess crop loss’
He ordered that relief measures be taken urgently in the waterlogged areas and steps initiated to assess the loss incurred by the agriculture sector so that compensation could be paid with contribution from the Central government.
The Chief Minister ordered that reservoirs across the State be filled with rainwater and called for plans to construct two barrages, one upstream and one downstream of Prakasam Barrage, to impound the local floodwaters and they be sent to the Centre for approval.
The officials told Mr. Naidu that there were no inflows into the Krishna and the rise in water level at Prakasam Barrage was due to the local floods.
Rainfall deficit
The officials explained that the overall rainfall deficit dropped from 50% to 31% due to recent rains. Coastal Andhra had 19.80% deficit while Rayalaseema 42% deficit. Though rains subsided for now, river inflows from upstream areas in North Andhra continued, they said.
The officials also informed the Chief Minister that water levels increased in 29 reservoirs. While the combined storage in these reservoirs stood at 101 tmc ft on September 23, it increased by around 21 tmc ft by September 26.
With inflows rising, surplus water being discharged downstream of Prakasam Barrage on Saturday.
| Photo Credit:
K.V.S. Giri
Rise in water levels
In the North Andhra districts, water levels in 11 projects increased by around 5 tmc ft and another 16 tmc ft increase was recorded in 18 reservoirs located in Kakinada, Polavaram, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Eluru, Palnadu, Nellore, Kurnool, Kadapa and Anantapur districts. Inflows in the Krishna, Godavari, Nagavali and Vamsadhara river basins increased significantly, they said.
Mr. Atchannaidu and officials briefed Mr. Naidu that inflows into the Gotta barrage increased from 7,214 cusecs on September 20 to 47,100 cusecs on September 25.
In the Nagavali basin, inflows into Narayanapuram anicut increased from 2,100 cusecs to 49,800 cusecs and in the Madduvvalasa project, inflows rose from 918 cusecs to around 18,000 cusecs.
The officials also reported that the inflows into the Thotapalli barrage increased from 2,484 cusecs to around 23,250 cusecs.
Storage in the Donkarayi reservoir increased from 11.67 tmc ft on September 20 to 15.78 tmc ft on September 25, while storage in the Sileru (Guntawada) reservoir rose from 1.52 tmc ft to 3.90 tmc ft.
Inflows at the Dowleswaram Barrage increased from 1.20 lakh cusecs on September 20 to 3.50 lakh cusecs on September 25. At Prakasam Barrage, inflows rose from 8,187 cusecs on September 20 to 40,521 cusecs on September 25.

Heavy rain halts Char Dham Yatra and shuts schools across Uttarakhand
Heavy rain forced Uttarakhand to suspend the Char Dham Yatra and close schools in several districts. Red and orange alerts have raised worries over landslides, road blockages and swelling rivers.

Heavy rain hits Uttarakhand, Char Dham Yatra suspended as red alert issued. (File image: PTI)
Heavy rain battered Uttarakhand on Saturday, leading the authorities to suspend the Char Dham Yatra till September 27 and shut schools in five districts. The India Meteorological Department issued a 'Red Alert' and an 'Orange Alert' for several parts of the state.
Rain has continued across most parts of Uttarakhand since morning, while higher areas saw intermittent snowfall. Officials said there were no reports so far of any casualties or major damage.
According to an order issued by Garhwal Commissioner Anand Swaroop, the Char Dham Yatra was suspended from the afternoon of September 26 until September 27 to ensure the safety of pilgrims. The Meteorological Department issued a 'Red Alert' for Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Champawat, Nainital and Udham Singh Nagar for Saturday. An 'Orange Alert' was issued for Dehradun, Pauri, Rudraprayag, Chamoli and Almora, while a 'Yellow Alert' was in place for Haridwar, Uttarkashi and Tehri.
As a precaution, schools up to Class 12 were closed in Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Champawat, Nainital and Rudraprayag. For Sunday, the department issued a 'Red Alert' for Dehradun, Tehri, Pauri and Haridwar, an 'Orange Alert' for Uttarkashi, Chamoli, Nainital and Rudraprayag, and a 'Yellow Alert' for Bageshwar, Almora, Champawat, Udham Singh Nagar and Pithoragarh. It has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall in several areas and extremely heavy rainfall at some places during this period.
The weather has increased the risk of landslides and road blockages in hilly areas, rising river levels and waterlogging in the plains. Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami appealed to people and tourists to remain vigilant and avoid unnecessary travel during the 'Red Alert' period. He also advised them not to go near rivers, streams and waterlogged areas. Dhami directed officials to stay alert and continuously monitor the water levels of rivers and streams, landslide-prone areas, hill roads, Char Dham routes and major tourist destinations. Overall, the state administration has stepped up precautions as heavy rain continues across Uttarakhand.
